items.description: Sec. 4 says 'See Figure 9 for domain sizes' (figure not available). The size is only implied by Table 2: h_c = 1/30 on a 60×30 mesh (fine mesh 1440×720) gives a 2×1 rectangle, assuming the 60 elements run along the beam axis. The text never says whether the whole rectangle is designable or contains a non-design support region.
readings: Full 2 × 1 rectangle (length 2 along x, height 1), entirely designable
2 × 1 rectangle containing a non-design support region drawn in Fig. 9 (e.g. a fixed circular region as in Michell's classical cantilever)

items.description: No sentence says where the beam is supported. Sec. 4 refers to Fig. 9 for the 'exact placement of boundaries'; only the word 'cantilever' implies one supported end.
readings: Entire left edge (x = 0, 0 ≤ y ≤ 1)
Only a central segment of the left edge
A circular/rigid clamped region near the left end (classical Michell cantilever)

items.description: The restraint type is not stated in the text; it appears only in Fig. 9 (Sec. 4).
readings: Fully clamped: u_x = u_y = 0 at all support nodes
Roller-type: u_x = 0 along the support plus a single u_y restraint

items.description: Sec. 4 only says the force is 'applied along a line of 1/10 L' in the Michell cantilever case. Which edge, at what height and how the line is oriented are given only in Fig. 9.
readings: Vertical segment on the right edge (x = 2) centred at mid-height (y = 0.5)
Horizontal row of nodes at mid-height (y = 0.5) ending at the right edge
Segment on the right edge starting at the bottom (or top) corner

items.description: L is never defined in the text (presumably in Fig. 9). Because the domain is 2×1, L could be the height or the length. With L = 1 the 0.1-long line covers 3 elements on the 60×30 mesh and cannot be centred on the mid-height node, so the set of loaded nodes is also open.
readings: 0.1 × domain length = 0.2 (6 / 12 / 24 elements)

items.entity: force distribution along the loaded line
items.description: 'The force is applied along a line' (Sec. 4) does not say whether this is a uniform traction (consistent nodal loads) or equal nodal point forces.
readings: Uniform traction converted to consistent nodal forces (end nodes at half weight)
Equal point forces on every node of the segment

items.description: The force direction is not stated anywhere in the text (Fig. 9 only). For a single load case the sign does not matter (C(-f) = C(f)), but the axis does.
readings: Vertical, transverse to the beam axis (up or down give the same optimum)
Inclined or horizontal (if Fig. 9 shows a component along the beam axis)

items.description: No force value is given anywhere. The tabulated compliances (e.g. C_ref = 106.21 in Table 2) depend on it.
readings: Total force F = 1 spread over the line
Unit traction per unit length (total 0.1 for L = 1)

items.description: V_max is never given as a number. The captions of Figs. 10–12 and App. A Fig. 1 say V = 0.25 / 0.40. Tables 2, 3 and A1 give reference volume fractions of 0.2532–0.2614 and 0.4023–0.4165, which rise with μmin. Eq. 1 constrains ρ^d, whose superscript is unexplained, and Sec. 4 sets ρ>0.99 and near-load elements to solid. It is therefore unclear which value is the actual constraint.
readings: V* = 0.25 and 0.40 exactly
V* = de-homogenized V_f (e.g. 0.2695, 0.4329) if matching the final one-scale designs

items.description: Sec. 4 says 'all elements with a density of ρ>0.99 and in a small radius around the load are set to solid'. The radius is not given. It is unclear whether this is a passive region during optimization or only a post-processing step, and whether 'and' joins two conditions or two separate rules.
readings: No passive region during optimization (solidification only in post-processing)
Passive solid disc around the load centre with radius ≈ half the loaded-line length (≈ 0.05)
Passive solid disc with radius ≈ 2–3 coarse elements (≈ 0.07–0.1)

items.description: No elastic modulus or thickness is given; only the void ratio α_out = 1e-9 appears (Sec. 2.1.1). The compliances in Tables 2, 3 and A1 scale with these values.
readings: E = 1 with unit thickness (normalized)
Physical values, e.g. E = 210 GPa with a specified thickness

items.description: ν is not stated anywhere in the paper.
Plane stress vs. plane strain is not stated. The choice changes the effective in-plane Poisson ratio.
readings: Plane stress
Plane strain

items.description: Sec. 4 gives 'a filter radius of r_min = 1.2 for varying mesh sizes' without units. It is unclear whether this means element widths on each mesh or a fixed physical length; a physical 1.2 would exceed the domain height of 1.
readings: 1.2 element widths of each coarse mesh (0.04 / 0.02 / 0.01 for 60×30 / 120×60 / 240×120)
Fixed physical radius 1.2 × (1/30) = 0.04 on all meshes
1.2 element widths of whatever mesh the single-scale solver uses (e.g. a fine mesh)

items.description: Eq. 2 only uses notation (tilde = filtered). The filter type, its weights, and which fields are filtered (μ1, μ2, s; θ?) are not given.
readings: Linear-hat density filter on μ1, μ2 and s
Sensitivity filter
Helmholtz (PDE) filter

items.description: Eqs. 1–4 use projected variables (bar) with superscripts k, d and e, probably eroded/dilated designs. No threshold η, sharpness β or continuation scheme is given, and the text doesn't say which design's compliance is minimized.
readings: Single tanh projection, η = 0.5, β continuation (e.g. 1 → 32)
Robust eroded/intermediate/dilated projections (e.g. η = 0.75/0.5/0.25), volume on dilated, area penalty on eroded
No projection (filtered densities only)

items.entity: objective normalization C_ref (with Γ = 0.05 area penalty)
items.description: Eq. 1 divides compliance by an undefined 'reference compliance' C_ref. The same symbol is used in Tables 2–3 for the converged homogenization compliance. With Γ = 0.05, the balance between compliance and the solid-area penalty depends on this value.
readings: C_ref = compliance of the initial design
C_ref = compliance of the fully solid domain
C_ref = a fixed constant such as the tabulated value (e.g. 106.21)

items.entity: material model / interpolation for a single-material solver
items.description: The reference uses rank-2 laminates whose closed-form properties are only cited ('see e.g. [9]', Sec. 2.1), plus the s-field scheme of [15] with μmin bounds (eqs. 1–4). The formulas are not given, and a single-material density solver has no μ/θ variables, so an interpolation must be chosen.
readings: Implement rank-2 laminate homogenization (μ1, μ2, θ, s) with μmin = 0.05/0.10/0.20, Γ = 0.05, γθ = 0
Standard SIMP with p = 3
Variable-thickness sheet (SIMP p = 1)

items.description: Sec. 4 only says eq. 1 'is solved until convergence'. The optimizer, move limits, tolerance and maximum iterations are not given.
readings: MMA, stop when max design change < 0.01
OC update (move limit 0.2), stop when change < 0.01
Fixed iteration count (e.g. 300–1000)

items.description: Starting values of μ1, μ2, s and θ (or of the density) are not given anywhere in Sec. 2.1 or Sec. 4.
readings: Uniform design at the volume bound, s = 1, θ from principal stresses of the uniform design
Uniform density = volume fraction, θ = 0

items.entity: optimization mesh for a single-scale re-run
items.description: Sec. 4.2 uses coarse homogenization meshes of 60×30 (Table 2), 120×60 (App. A) and 240×120 (Table 3), plus fine meshes of 1440×720, 2400×1200, 2880×1440 and 5760×2880. It doesn't say which one defines the example for a single-scale solver.
readings: Fine one-scale resolution, e.g. 1440×720 or 2400×1200

items.description: The element type and order are not stated; only square elements are implied by h_c.
readings: 4-node bilinear quadrilateral (Q4)
Higher-order quadrilateral (8- or 9-node)
